topic: Someone receives a package intended for the previous tenant
text: I stare at the package, the handwriting unfamiliar, the name not mine. It’s one of those moments when the quiet of your home feels suddenly exposed, like a whispered secret that’s been shouted. I hesitate, the box resting heavily on my hands. It’s not meant for me, this bundle of someone else’s life, but the weight of it presses down as if it’s mine to carry. I shouldn’t open it, yet the curiosity, the inexplicable pull, makes me consider breaking the seal. What stories lie inside, wrapped and waiting? But to do so feels like an intrusion, a step into territory not mine. I set it down, the silence around me deepening, and step back, letting the space between us grow.
